title.en: Hikers feared missing after 'terrifying' flash flooding hits Grand Canyon
title.zh: 大峡谷发生“可怕”的洪水，登山者失踪

summary.en: More than 20 people are thought to be unaccounted for after flash flooding on Saturday.
summary.zh: 周六，山洪暴发，据信有20多人失踪。

body.en:
More than 20 people are thought to be missing or unaccounted for after flash flooding swept through parts of the Grand Canyon.

It hit at around 14:30 local time (22:30 BST) on Saturday in Bright Angel Canyon and Phantom Ranch area, according to the National Park Service (NPS).

Sixty-two people have so far been airlifted out of the area, with more expected to follow. No injuries have been reported.

"The whole thing was terrifying," said Nikki Baggs, 41, who was among those to be airlifted out of the bottom of the Grand Canyon on Saturday alongside her two friends.

"It was a beautiful day and then people were screaming, running," she told the BBC.

Baggs said she and her friends had just dropped off their belongings at a cabin in Phantom Ranch - a remote lodge at the bottom of the Grand Canyon - when they decided to venture out to enjoy the nice day. Before they knew it, a flood of water was sweeping through the area.

As soon as the rain hit, Baggs and her friends headed toward higher ground, where they sat at a picnic table, before rangers yelled to them to run again to a different ledge, where they waited with others for hours before they were evacuated at around 21:30 local time.

Baggs said she and her two friends had been looking forward to a steak dinner at Phantom Ranch - but were now just grateful to be alive thanks to a swift response from park rangers.

"It was a really uniquely coordinated effort," she said. "That's what made us feel safe about all of it in an unsafe situation."

The NPS said flooding had caused significant damage in some areas and that trails in the area have been closed. Baggs said she and her friends watched from higher ground as bridges were swept away.

It asked anyone who knew of hikers or backpackers who were in the inner canyon along the Bright Angel Creek corridor on Saturday to get in touch.

It also warned that more thunderstorms and heavy rainfall were forecast for Sunday and Monday, which could lead to "additional flash flooding, debris flows, rockfall and changing trail and river conditions".

The Grand Canyon is one of the most popular national parks in the US, with about five million people visiting each year. The Bright Angel trail is its most popular hike.
body.zh: 山洪席卷大峡谷部分地区后，据信有 20 多人失踪或下落不明。 据国家公园管理局 (NPS) 称，周六当地时间 14:30 左右（英国夏令时 22:30），袭击发生在光明天使峡谷和幻影牧场地区。 迄今为止，已有 62 人被空运出该地区，预计还会有更多人跟进。目前还没有人员受伤的报告。 “整件事太可怕了，”41 岁的尼基·巴格斯 (Nikki Baggs) 说，她是周六与她的两个朋友一起从大峡谷底部被空运出来的人之一。 “那是美好的一天，然后人们尖叫着、奔跑着，”她告诉英国广播公司。 巴格斯说，她和她的朋友们刚刚把行李放在幻影牧场（大峡谷底部的一个偏远小屋）的一间小屋里，然后决定出去享受美好的一天。在他们意识到之前，洪水席卷了整个地区。 雨一落下，巴格斯和她的朋友们就向地势较高的地方走去，她们坐在野餐桌旁，然后护林员向她们喊叫，让她们再次跑到另一个窗台上，她们和其他人在那里等了几个小时，然后在当地时间 21:30 左右被疏散。 巴格斯说，她和她的两个朋友一直期待着在幻影牧场吃牛排晚餐，但现在很庆幸自己还活着，多亏了公园管理员的迅速反应。 “这是一次真正独特的协调努力，”她说。 “这就是让我们在不安全的情况下感到安全的原因。” NPS 表示，洪水对一些地区造成了严重破坏，该地区的步道已关闭。巴格斯说，她和她的朋友们在地势较高的地方看着桥梁被冲走。 它要求任何认识周六在光明天使溪走廊沿线的内峡谷徒步旅行者或背包客的人与我们联系。 它还警告称，预计周日和周一将出现更多雷暴和强降雨，这可能导致“额外的山洪、泥石流、落石以及步道和河流状况的变化”。 大峡谷是美国最受欢迎的国家公园之一，每年约有 500 万人参观。光明天使步道是最受欢迎的徒步路线。

reflection.en: The Grand Canyon, a place of immense natural beauty, can also become a scene of terrifying power, as seen with the recent flash floods. In moments of overwhelming crisis, when the earth itself seems to tremble, we can find refuge and strength in Yahweh. He is our ever-present help in times of trouble, a steadfast anchor amidst the chaos.
reflection.zh: 大峡谷是一个自然美景极其壮丽的地方，但正如最近的洪水所示，它也可能变成一个充满可怕力量的场景。在压倒性的危机时刻，当地球本身似乎在颤抖时，我们可以在雅伟那里找到避难所和力量。祂是我们患难中随时的帮助，是混乱中的坚定锚。

verse.textEn: God is our refuge and strength, an ever-present help in trouble.
verse.textZh: 神是我们的避难所，是我们的力量，是我们在患难中随时的帮助。

title.en: Number of missing Australians in Nepal rises, as China links disaster to climate change
title.zh: 尼泊尔失踪澳大利亚人数量上升，中国将灾害与气候变化联系起来

summary.en: Australians have raised millions of dollars for survivors of a disaster in Nepal, where the death toll has risen to nearly 800 and over 3,000 people remain missing after a torrent of ice, rock, mud, and debris swept through mountain valleys. The Australian government has committed $8 million in total humanitarian...
summary.zh: 尼泊尔发生灾难后，澳大利亚人为幸存者筹集了数百万美元。一场冰、岩石、泥土和碎屑的洪流席卷了山谷，导致近800人死亡，超过3000人失踪。澳大利亚政府已承诺提供总计800万美元的人道主义援助。

body.en:
Australians have raised millions of dollars to assist survivors of the Nepal disaster, with many forced into temporary shelters amid mud and chaos.

Authorities said the death toll rose to nearly 800 on Sunday, with more than 3,000 people missing on both sides of the Nepal-China border after a torrent of ice, rock, mud and debris swept through mountain valleys and rivers on Wednesday, causing widespread devastation.

The federal government has announced a further $3 million in humanitarian support for Nepal, including supplies transported by the Australian Defence Force. It brings Australia's total assistance to $8 million.

The survivors remain in desperate need of basic amenities like clean drinking water and medical supplies.

Among them, Rabindra Hamal told the Australian Associated Press (AAP) news agency he and his colleagues working at a dam site were told to flee just minutes before the flood hit their area on Wednesday.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

They made their escape by car, but as they later tried to reach higher ground by foot, two of the group were swept away.

The group continued to scramble to safety but were forced to wait until the following day to be rescued.

They were flown by helicopter to a nearby army barracks and then evacuated to Kathmandu.

Hamal said that of the several thousand people working on the hydro project, about 500 were still missing.

As of Sunday evening, the number of missing Australians rose to 43, with the federal government continuing to do everything possible to confirm their welfare.

A public candlelight vigil will be held at Melbourne's Federation Square on Monday evening, in memory of those lost in the disaster.

A joint call for aid from the Emergency Action Alliance (EAA), made up of 15 prominent charities, has raised more than $3.5 million, including $2 million in contributions from the federal government.

The funding is going towards providing much-needed emergency shelter, food, safe drinking water, healthcare, hygiene and sanitation services, and supporting longer-term recovery assistance.

Save the Children is one of the organisations participating in the alliance, with the group's global media manager Amy Lefevre, visiting the affected Nuwakot district on Saturday.

"It's just mud everywhere, there's also a lot of confusion and chaos," she told AAP.

"It's just incredibly sad when you look around and you see someone's shoes stuck in the mud, or people's belongings strewn everywhere.

"It's very much still a rescue operation but of course, today is day five, and I think the chance of finding people alive is slowly dimming."

body.zh: 澳大利亚人筹集了数百万美元来援助尼泊尔灾难的幸存者，许多人在泥泞和混乱中被迫进入临时避难所。 当局表示，周三冰块、岩石、泥浆和碎片席卷山谷和河流，造成大范围破坏，周日死亡人数上升至近800人，中尼边境两侧有3000多人失踪。 联邦政府宣布向尼泊尔再提供300万美元的人道主义支持，其中包括澳大利亚国防军运送的物资。这使得澳大利亚的援助总额达到 800 万美元。 幸存者仍然迫切需要清洁饮用水和医疗用品等基本设施。 其中，拉宾德拉·哈马尔 (Rabindra Hamal) 告诉澳大利亚美联社 (AAP)，周三洪水袭击他们所在地区的几分钟前，他和在水坝工地工作的同事被告知逃离。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 他们乘汽车逃跑，但当他们后来试图步行到达更高的地方时，其中两人被卷走了。 这群人继续爬向安全地带，但被迫等到第二天才获救。 他们乘坐直升机飞往附近的军营，然后疏散到加德满都。 哈马尔表示，在水电项目上工作的数千人中，仍有约 500 人失踪。 截至周日晚上，失踪的澳大利亚人人数上升至43人，联邦政府继续尽一切可能确认他们的福利。 周一晚上，墨尔本联邦广场将举行公众烛光守夜活动，以纪念在灾难中丧生的人们。 由 15 个知名慈善机构组成的紧急行动联盟 (EAA) 联合呼吁提供援助，已筹集了超过 350 万美元，其中包括联邦政府的 200 万美元捐款。 这笔资金将用于提供急需的紧急住所、食品、安全饮用水、医疗保健、卫生和环境卫生服务，并支持长期恢复援助。 救助儿童会是参与该联盟的组织之一，该组织的全球媒体经理 Amy Lefevre 于周六访问了受影响的努瓦科特地区。 她告诉澳联社：“到处都是泥巴，还有很多混乱和混乱。” “当你环顾四周，看到有人的鞋子陷在泥里，或者人们的财物散落各处时，真是令人难以置信的悲伤。 “这仍然是一次救援行动，但当然，今天已经是第五天了，我认为找到生还者的机会正在慢慢变小。” 对于那些幸存下来的人来说，许多家庭都被撕裂了……

reflection.en: The news of Australians raising millions for Nepal disaster survivors, who are in desperate need of basic amenities, reminds us of the profound call to care for those suffering. Yahweh teaches that when we extend compassion to the "least of these" — those displaced and grieving after a torrent of ice and mud — we are, in essence, serving Him directly. This...
reflection.zh: 澳大利亚人为尼泊尔灾难幸存者筹集数百万美元，他们急需基本生活用品，这提醒我们关怀受苦之人的深刻呼召。雅伟教导我们，当我们向“这些最小的弟兄”——那些在冰雪泥石流后流离失所、悲痛欲绝的人——施以怜悯时，我们实际上是在直接服侍祂。这种集体的慷慨在巨大悲剧面前，表达了切实的爱。

verse.textEn: Truly I tell you, whatever you did for one of the least of these brothers and sisters of mine, you did for me.
verse.textZh: 我实在告诉你们，这些事你们既做在我这弟兄中一个最小的身上，就是做在我身上了。

title.en: US strikes Iranian launchers on Larak Island in first known attack in weeks
title.zh: 美国袭击了拉拉克岛的伊朗发射器，这是数周以来首次已知的袭击

summary.en: Iran says the attack killed some civilians and is the first known US strike on Iran since late July.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
US forces have struck two Iranian launchers on Iran's Larak island, a US official said, marking the first known American strikes on Iran since late July.

"Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) forces were observed preparing to launch rockets with sea mines into Strait of Hormuz," the BBC's US partner CBS News quoted US Central Command spokesman Cdr Tim Hawkins as saying.

The IRGC said the attack on Sunday killed and wounded several people, and vowed "response and punishment".

It marks the first known US strike in Iran since US President Donald Trump paused a renewed military campaign in late July. The US said it had finished clearing all mines from the strait's main shipping lane earlier this month.

Larak Island is just offshore from the key port of Bandar Abbas and sits right on the Strait of Hormuz, a vital waterway for global shipping.

Iran is currently making tanker traffic pass by this island for checking and reportedly forcing vessels to pay $2m (£1.5m) to cross.

Hossein Mohebbi, the IRGC's spokesman called the attack a "strategic and fatal mistake by the Trump regime" and said that the "enemy will pay the consequences of this miscalculation in both the economic and military fields".

Iran's Tasnim news agency, which is affiliated with the IRGC, said earlier that the attack was carried out by drones. Reports indicate that two people were killed and two others injured, it said.

Trump ​said last week that all mines‌ placed in the Strait of Hormuz by Iran as part of its efforts to blockade the route had been detonated or removed. He said Iran had been warned that any ship ​or boat deploying new mines would be ​destroyed.

Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi described Trump's claim as a "propaganda" deception.

Iran is facing renewed economic pressure after Washington announced a fresh sanctions campaign on 24 August aimed at further isolating Tehran and expanding secondary sanctions against its allies .

Iranian officials and state media have largely dismissed the campaign as a continuation of previous US economic measures, which they argue followed Washington's military failure in the recent conflict.

The US and Israel launched wide-ranging strikes on Iran on 28 February, with Iran responding by attacking Israel, US bases and allied states in the Gulf, and effectively closing the Strait of Hormuz to marine traffic. The Iran war has now crossed its six-month mark.

Some 20% of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas used to travel through before the war began.
body.zh: 一名美国官员表示，美国军队袭击了伊朗拉拉克岛的两座伊朗发射器，这是自 7 月底以来美国首次对伊朗发动袭击。 英国广播公司美国合作伙伴哥伦比亚广播公司新闻援引美国中央司令部发言人蒂姆·霍金斯中校的话说：“据观察，伊斯兰革命卫队（IRGC）部队准备向霍尔木兹海峡发射带有水雷的火箭。” 伊朗伊斯兰革命卫队表示，周日的袭击造成多人死亡和受伤，并誓言“做出回应和惩罚”。 这是自美国总统唐纳德·特朗普7月下旬暂停新的军事行动以来美国首次对伊朗发动袭击。美国表示，本月早些时候已完成该海峡主要航道上的所有水雷清除工作。 拉拉克岛位于阿巴斯港主要港口的近海处，坐落在全球航运的重要水道霍尔木兹海峡上。 伊朗目前正在让油轮通过该岛进行检查，据报道，伊朗迫使船只支付 200 万美元（150 万英镑）的费用。 伊斯兰革命卫队发言人侯赛因·莫赫比称这次袭击是“特朗普政权的战略性致命错误”，并表示“敌人将为这种经济和军事领域误判的后果付出代价”。 隶属于伊斯兰革命卫队的伊朗塔斯尼姆通讯社早些时候表示，此次袭击是由无人机实施的。报道称，两人死亡，两人受伤。 特朗普上周表示，伊朗为封锁霍尔木兹海峡而埋设的所有地雷均已被引爆或清除。他说，伊朗已收到警告，任何部署新水雷的船只都将被摧毁。 伊朗副外长卡泽姆·加里巴迪称特朗普的说法是“宣传”欺骗。 华盛顿于8月24日宣布采取新的制裁行动，旨在进一步孤立德黑兰并扩大对其盟友的二级制裁后，伊朗面临着新的经济压力。 伊朗官员和官方媒体在很大程度上驳斥了这一行动，认为这是美国之前经济措施的延续，他们认为这些措施是在华盛顿在最近的冲突中军事失败之后采取的。 2月28日，美国和以色列对伊朗发动了大范围的打击，伊朗的回应是攻击以色列、美国基地和海湾盟国，并有效关闭了霍尔木兹海峡的海上交通。伊朗战争现已突破六个月大关。 战争开始前，世界上约 20% 的石油和液化天然气都经过这里运输。

reflection.en: This story draws attention to peace-making and restraint. Matthew 5:9 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with mercy, truth, and restraint, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到和平与克制。Matthew 5:9提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以怜悯、真实与节制来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

verse.textEn: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God.
verse.textZh: 使人和睦的人有福了，因为他们必称为神的儿子。

title.en: USDA reportedly shelves cyclospora research amid relocations and fund cuts

title.en: US military launches first strike on Iranian forces near Hormuz since July
title.zh: 美国对霍尔木兹海峡附近的伊朗军队发动自七月以来的首次打击

summary.en: US forces struck two Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz after observing preparations to target shipping with sea mines. Iran has since promised to retaliate for the strike, marking the first such military action in the region since late July.
summary.zh: 美国军队袭击了霍尔木兹海峡拉拉克岛上的两个伊朗火箭发射器，此前观察到对方正准备用海矿袭击航运。伊朗随后承诺对此次袭击进行报复，这是自7月底以来该地区首次发生此类军事行动。

body.en:
US forces have struck two Iranian rocket launchers on the Strait of Hormuz in the first military action since late July, a US official said Monday.

"I can confirm that earlier today US forces struck two Iranian launchers on Larak Island. Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps forces were observed preparing to launch rockets with sea mines into Strait of Hormuz," the US official said.

Semiofficial news outlets in Iran reported sounds of explosions near Larak island on the strait.

Forces with the Revolutionary Guard Corps were observed preparing to launch rockets with sea mines into the strait, according to the official, who spoke on condition of anonymity to detail sensitive military movements.

The US military last week completed clearing sea mines from the strait’s international shipping routes.

title.en: Eight killed and others missing after ferry capsizes off northern Cyprus
title.zh: 塞浦路斯北部渡轮倾覆，八人死亡，多人失踪

summary.en: A search and rescue operation is under way after a ferry carrying nearly 270 people turns over after leaving port.
summary.zh: 一艘载有近270人的渡轮在离港后倾覆，目前正在进行搜救行动。

body.en:
At least eight people have died and more than a dozen others are still missing after a passenger boat capsized off northern Cyprus, the head of the Turkish administration there has said.

Ünal Üstel, prime minister of the self-proclaimed Turkish republic on Cyprus, said the ferry had been carrying 259 passengers and eight crew members when it began taking on water after departing the coastal town of Kyrenia.

The ship's captain and seven crew members have been detained as part of an investigation into "how this tragedy occurred", Üstel wrote on social media.

A search and rescue operation to find the passengers still unaccounted for is under way, which Turkish authorities have joined.

The privately owned ferry left the left the popular holiday resort of Kyrenia at about 12:30 local time (09:30 GMT).

Üstel said the boat had been scheduled to travel to Turkey on Saturday, but had been delayed due to poor weather conditions.

He told Turkish media outlet TRT that the boat was hit by two waves before it capsized.

While the captain of the vessel was trying to recover from the first wave, a second wave hit and it began taking on water, he told the outlet.

Helicopters and coastguard boats have been dispatched to the scene, while ambulances have been stationed on the beach ready to receive rescued passengers.

Üstel wrote on social media that the "priority right now is human life", adding that security forces, rescue teams and health officials were all on the scene.

He added the disaster will be thoroughly investigated and "even the slightest negligence will be uncovered".

"No one will be spared, regardless of who they are, who is found to be at fault or responsible," Üstel said.

Erhan Arikli, the transport minister of the self-declared Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus (TRNC), which is only recognised by Turkey, told local media that 100 passengers had been taken to shore.

Turkey's President Recep Tayyip Erdogan sent his condolences to Turkish Cypriots and said efforts to reach those who were still missing "continue uninterrupted".

"Immediately after the accident, we launched extensive search-and-rescue operations in co-operation with the authorities of the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus," he said at a military ceremony on Sunday.

Mustafa Koc saved around 65 people with his boat after the vessel capsized. He told the BBC that he felt the crew should have waited until the sea was calm.

He said the boat had arrived in Kyrenia on Saturday and "had some damage in the front".

The ferry - a high-speed 40m long, 10m wide Filo Jet vessel - sails under the flag of Turkey, according to Marine Traffic.

Filo Denizcilik, the company which operates the capsized passenger boat, said it was "deeply saddened by the tragic accident".

title.en: What the case of a slain Australian reveals about accountability for 'mistakes'
title.zh: 一名被杀的澳大利亚人的案件揭示了“错误”的责任

summary.en: An investigation into Zomi Frankcom's death is closed. But important questions remain unanswered.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Share your feedback and help us improve this feature. Read more about how we use AI at SBS here.

In the case of Zomi Frankcom , an Australian killed in a drone strike while delivering humanitarian aid to the Gaza Strip in 2024, Israel's military justice system has concluded there is no reasonable suspicion of criminal misconduct.

It announced this month its decision to close the investigation into the death of Frankcom and six other World Central Kitchen (WCK) colleagues.

Israel's ambassador to Australia, Hillel Newman, said there had been no intention to attack the aid workers and a "reasonable mistake" was made.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

"There are tragic circumstances in a war zone and we're very sorry for the family, but that does not always mean that there's criminal liability," Newman told ABC Radio National.

Two Israel Defense Forces (IDF) officers were removed from their positions over the incident and another three were formally reprimanded.

But Foreign Minister Penny Wong has criticised the decision, noting "there are still many unanswered questions".

The Frankcom family and WCK are demanding an independent investigation into the airstrikes, saying "the IDF cannot credibly investigate its own conduct".

The case raises questions about whether Israel's military justice system is capable of delivering fair outcomes when its forces are accused of killing civilians, and where the line lies between a tragic operational error and conduct that warrants criminal investigation.

Michelle Burgis-Kasthala, professor of international law at La Trobe University, says there is "very compelling documentation" from many human rights organisations to suggest a "pattern of impunity" when it comes to the investigation of war crimes in Israel.

"A lot of the time they simply lapse and very rarely do they ever result in any form of criminal investigation, and even less likely [to result in] criminal conviction."

Last year, Action on Armed Violence (AOAV) looked at 52 publicly reported incidents in English-language media between October 2023 and June 2025, in which the Israeli media either reported an investigation was underway, or serious allegations of civilian harm.

The London-based charity found 88 per cent were either still under review or had been closed without any finding of wrongdoing.

So far, according to the cases examined by AOAV, only one case has resulted in a prison sentence against the accused.

title.en: 'A giant leap forward': Nasa launches powerful new space telescope
title.zh: “巨大的飞跃”：美国宇航局发射强大的新型太空望远镜

summary.en: The US space agency's telescope is starting a multi-year mission to create a new map of the universe and learn more about dark energy and dark matter.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及智慧、知识与追求真理。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Nasa's powerful next-generation telescope has blasted off into space from its launchpad in Florida, with a mission to explore dark energy, black holes and other mysteries of the Universe.

The Nancy Grace Roman telescope will capture vast panoramic views of space, with a field of vision 100 times larger than both the Hubble and James Webb space telescopes, Nasa says.

The mission begins with a 100-day journey to a vantage point roughly one million miles from Earth, where the telescope will then start charting planets outside our solar system, known as exoplanets.

"Roman is going to change the way we look at the Universe," said Nicky Fox, a Nasa administrator.

The successful launch of the telescope took place on Sunday morning local time from the Kennedy Space Center in Florida.

Jackie Townsend, a project manager on Nasa's Roman telescope, described it as "glorious" at a news conference afterwards. "The ride was magnificent. It put us right where we wanted to be."

About 30 minutes after launch, Roman separated from its SpaceX rocket and is now heading towards its orbiting point around a million miles away.

Fox said Roman "is going to discover tens of thousands, maybe even 100,000 new exoplanets" - referring to planets located outside of our solar system.

"Why do we care so much about exoplanets? Because one of our main goals at Nasa is answering the question, 'Are we alone in the universe'?" she added.

US President Donald Trump dialled in to the space agency's news conference to congratulate the scientists working on the project.

"You're the hottest in space, and we have the hottest country anywhere in the world. So, let's keep it all going. You're a big part of it," Trump said.

Astronomer Jenifer Millard said the telescope will be four times further from Earth than the Moon is, where a lot of infrared space cameras - made to pick up what she describes as "heat light"- operate.

She told the BBC this is to make sure infrared light from the Moon and Earth don't interfere with the cameras.

Nasa's James Webb Space Telescope, launched in 2021, also orbits the Sun around one million miles from Earth, but its field of vision is not as expansive. Nasa's Hubble Space Telescope, launched in 1990, orbits at about 300 miles above Earth's surface.

While Roman will look outward into the Universe, Millard said scientists are also anticipating it will find thousands of new worlds in our own galaxy.

The telescope is named after physicist Nancy Grace Roman, who was Nasa's first chief astronomer in the 1960s and its first female executive.

During her career, she was instrumental in getting the Hubble Space Telescope approved by US Congress and later said its most interesting discovery was dark energy.

body.zh: 美国宇航局强大的下一代望远镜已从佛罗里达州的发射台发射升空，其任务是探索暗能量、黑洞和宇宙的其他奥秘。 美国宇航局表示，南希·格雷斯·罗曼望远镜将捕捉广阔的太空全景，其视野比哈勃和詹姆斯·韦伯太空望远镜大100倍。 该任务从为期 100 天的旅程开始，到达距地球约 100 万英里的有利位置，然后望远镜将开始绘制太阳系外行星（称为系外行星）的图表。 “罗曼将改变我们看待宇宙的方式，”美国宇航局管理员尼基福克斯说。 该望远镜于当地时间周日上午在佛罗里达州肯尼迪航天中心成功发射。 美国宇航局罗马望远镜的项目经理杰基·汤森德在随后的新闻发布会上形容这是“光荣的”。 “这次旅程非常棒。它让我们到达了我们想去的地方。” 发射后约 30 分钟，Roman 与 SpaceX 火箭分离，目前正朝着约 100 万英里外的轨道点前进。 福克斯表示，罗曼“将发现数万颗，甚至可能是 10 万颗新的系外行星”——指的是位于太阳系之外的行星。 “为什么我们如此关心系外行星？因为美国宇航局的主要目标之一就是回答这个问题：‘我们在宇宙中孤独吗？’”她补充道。 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普拨通了航天局的新闻发布会，向从事该项目的科学家表示祝贺。 “你们是太空中最热门的国家，我们拥有世界上最热门的国家。所以，让我们继续努力。你们是其中的重要组成部分，”特朗普说。 天文学家詹妮弗·米勒德表示，这架望远镜距离地球的距离将是月球距离的四倍，月球上有许多红外太空相机，用于捕捉她所说的“热光”。 她告诉英国广播公司，这是为了确保来自月球和地球的红外光不会干扰相机。 美国宇航局 (NASA) 的詹姆斯·韦伯太空望远镜于 2021 年发射，也绕太阳运行，距地球约 100 万英里，但其视野没有那么广阔。美国宇航局的哈勃太空望远镜于 1990 年发射，其轨道距地球表面约 300 英里。 米勒德表示，虽然罗曼将向外观察宇宙，但科学家们也预计它将在我们自己的星系中发现数千个新世界。 该望远镜以物理学家南希·格雷斯·罗曼 (Nancy Grace Roman) 的名字命名，她是 20 世纪 60 年代美国宇航局第一位首席天文学家，也是第一位女性高管。 在她的职业生涯中，她在哈勃太空望远镜获得美国国会批准方面发挥了重要作用，后来表示其最有趣的发现是暗能量。 新望远镜同样有望...

title.en: Guinea-Bissau votes to reshape presidency
title.zh: 几内亚比绍投票重塑总统制

summary.en: Guinea-Bissau's military government held a referendum to amend the constitution, aiming to grant more powers to the president, ahead of planned elections in December. The opposition called for a boycott, leading to low voter turnout.
summary.zh: 几内亚比绍军政府举行了一次修宪公投，旨在赋予总统更多权力，此前该国计划于12月举行选举。反对派呼吁抵制，导致投票率较低。

body.en:
The West African nation's military government wants to amend the constitution to give more powers to the president. The junta, which seized power last year, says it will hold elections in December.

Guinea-Bissau voted on Sunday in a referendum on whether to give the president new powers as the country prepares to transition from military to democratic rule.

According to the Associated Press, many polling stations had low turnout after the opposition urged voters to boycott the referendum.

The tiny West African nation of around 2.2 million people has been under army rule since last November following a disputed election.

Guinea-Bissau's junta has unanimously approved a constitutional amendment to switch the country from what it frames as a parliamentary to a presidential system.

This means abandoning the old system where the prime minister came from the parliamentary majority. 

The amendment would allow the president to appoint and dismiss the prime minister and dissolve parliament.

If passed, the new constitution will cut the number of seats in parliament from 102 to 65.

The junta says the change seeks to stabilize institutions before new presidential and parliamentary elections, scheduled for December 6, which are meant to hand power back to civilians.

Opposition groups, however, have urged the public to boycott the vote, saying it will allow the junta leader to cement power and calling it a "source of political instability at all levels."

Polls close at 1700 GMT on Sunday, with the first provisional results due from Tuesday.

One of the world's poorest countries, Guinea-Bissau has experienced five coups and a series of attempted coups since 1974.

A military government seized power in November following a disputed election in which former President Umaro Sissoco Embalo and opposition candidate Fernando Dias both claimed victory.

After legislative elections in 2023, Embalo himself dissolved the opposition-dominated parliament in response to what he described as an attempted coup.

If you rely on our team for trusted reporting, please take a moment to select us as your Preferred Source on Google so you'll always see our verified news first.
body.zh: 这个西非国家的军政府希望修改宪法，赋予总统更多权力。去年掌权的军政府表示将于 12 月举行选举。 几内亚比绍周日举行全民公投，决定是否赋予总统新权力，因为该国准备从军事统治过渡到民主统治。 据美联社报道，在反对派敦促选民抵制公投后，许多投票站的投票率很低。 这个拥有约 220 万人口的西非小国自去年 11 月一场有争议的选举以来一直处于军队统治之下。 几内亚比绍军政府一致批准了一项宪法修正案，将该国从议会制转变为总统制。 这意味着放弃总理来自议会多数的旧制度。 该修正案将允许总统任命和罢免总理以及解散议会。 如果新宪法获得通过，议会席位将从 102 个削减至 65 个。 军政府表示，这一变化旨在在定于 12 月 6 日举行的新总统和议会选举之前稳定机构，选举的目的是将权力交还给平民。 然而，反对派团体敦促公众抵制这次投票，称这将使军政府领导人巩固权力，并称其为“各级政治不稳定的根源”。 投票于周日格林威治标准时间 1700 点结束，第一个临时结果将于周二公布。 几内亚比绍是世界上最贫穷的国家之一，自 1974 年以来经历了五次政变和一系列未遂政变。 11 月，在一场有争议的选举中，前总统乌马罗·西索科·恩巴洛和反对派候选人费尔南多·迪亚斯双双宣布获胜，军政府夺取了权力。 2023 年立法选举后，恩巴洛本人解散了反对派主导的议会，以回应他所说的未遂政变。 如果您信赖我们团队的可信报道，请花点时间选择我们作为您在 Google 上的首选来源，以便您始终能够首先看到我们经过验证的新闻。

Yahweh's word warns against rulers who, like roaring lions, prey on their helpless people. As the nation prepares for elections, the low voter turnout in the referendum suggests a...

title.en: Greece, Turkey clash over protected Aegean marine areas
title.zh: 希腊和土耳其就受保护的爱琴海海洋区域发生冲突

summary.en: Turkey's announcement of two protected zones in a disputed Aegean Sea area has sparked an angry reaction from Greece, potentially marking a new chapter in their long-running dispute after a brief period of improved relations.
summary.zh: 土耳其宣布在爱琴海争议区域设立两个保护区，引发希腊强烈反应，这可能标志着两国在短暂改善关系后，长期争端进入新篇章。

body.en:
Turkey has announced the creation of two protected zones in a disputed area of the Aegean Sea, sparking an angry reaction from Greece. Does this mark a new chapter in a long-running dispute between the two countries?

A stint of unfamiliar calm between Greece and Turkey lasted less than three years.

After a devastating earthquake struck Turkey in February 2023 and Greece provided substantial aid, the two countries came closer together. They then signed the Athens Declaration on Friendly Relations and Good-Neighbourliness in December 2023, a further step to improved relations.

During this unusual time of calm, neither government moved to resolve long-lasting Greek-Turkish disputes, which mostly involve  marking maritime boundaries . As a result, even a measure ostensibly aimed at protecting the environment has reignited regional tensions.

The latest dispute was triggered by Turkey's designation of two marine parks in the Aegean Sea and eastern Mediterranean earlier this month. The park in the northeastern Aegean includes a protected area in the waters between the Greek islands of Lemnos and Samothrace. The southern park lies east of Rhodes and surrounds the Greek island of Kastellorizo.

For decades, Greece and Turkey have been at odds over the delineation of their maritime borders in the Aegean and the related economic rights, such as claims to natural resources like oil .

Greece's Foreign Ministry was quick to react to the announcement, calling the establishment of the parks "illegal." In a statement, it said the designation of Turkish marine parks in areas outside Turkey's territorial waters has no legal validity.

Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis  said at a Cabinet meeting earlier this week that he wanted to maintain good relations with neighboring countries. However, he stressed that "areas under Greek sovereignty are determined by international law" and that Greece is "always ready to defend them."

For its part, Greece also announced two marine parks in 2025 — in the Ionian Islands and the southern Cyclades, both within Greek territorial waters. At the time, Turkey reacted in a clearly worded statement: "Unilateral actions should be avoided in closed or semi-closed seas such as the Aegean and the Mediterranean."

But Turkey has now declared its own marine parks — and without consulting Greece. Environmental protection appears to have been, at most, a secondary concern for the two countries in announcing their respective conservation parks. Instead, the move appears to be a new tactic for asserting dominance in the disputed maritime area — the latest chapter in a decades-long regional spat.

Greece believes Turkey sees the marine...
body.zh: 土耳其宣布在爱琴海争议海域设立两个保护区，引发希腊愤怒反应。这是否标志着两国之间长期争端翻开了新的篇章？ 希腊和土耳其之间一段不寻常的平静持续了不到三年。 2023 年 2 月土耳其发生毁灭性地震，希腊提供了大量援助后，两国关系更加紧密。随后，他们于 2023 年 12 月签署了《雅典友好关系和睦邻宣言》，为改善关系又迈出了一步。 在这段不同寻常的平静时期，两国政府都没有采取行动解决长期存在的希腊与土耳其争端，这些争端主要涉及划定海上边界。结果，即使是表面上旨在保护环境的措施也重新引发了地区紧张局势。 最新的争端是由土耳其本月早些时候指定爱琴海和东地中海的两个海洋公园引发的。该公园位于爱琴海东北部，包括希腊利姆诺斯岛和萨莫色雷斯岛之间水域的保护区。南部公园位于罗德岛东部，环绕希腊卡斯特洛里佐岛。 几十年来，希腊和土耳其在爱琴海海上边界的划定以及相关经济权利（例如对石油等自然资源的主张）方面一直存在分歧。 希腊外交部迅速对此公告做出反应，称建立公园是“非法的”。它在一份声明中表示，在土耳其领海以外地区指定土耳其海洋公园没有法律效力。 希腊总理基里亚科斯·米佐塔基斯在本周早些时候的内阁会议上表示，他希望与邻国保持良好关系。不过，他强调，“希腊主权范围是由国际法决定的”，希腊“随时准备保卫这些地区”。 希腊还宣布将于 2025 年在爱奥尼亚群岛和基克拉泽斯群岛南部建立两个海洋公园，两者均位于希腊领海内。当时，土耳其在一份措辞明确的声明中做出回应：“应避免在爱琴海和地中海等封闭或半封闭海域采取单方面行动。” 但土耳其现在已经宣布建立自己的海洋公园，而且没有咨询希腊。在两国宣布各自的保护公园时，环境保护似乎最多只是次要问题。相反，此举似乎是在有争议的海域主张主导地位的新策略——这是长达数十年的地区争端的最新篇章。 希腊相信土耳其看到了海洋...

reflection.en: The recent clash between Greece and Turkey over protected marine areas in the Aegean Sea reminds us how quickly old divisions can resurface, even after a period of calm and declarations of friendly relations. Ephesians 2:14 speaks of Yahweh breaking down 'the dividing wall of hostility' between groups, a profound hope for nations with long-running disputes....
reflection.zh: 希腊和土耳其最近在爱琴海有争议海域设立保护区而引发的冲突，提醒我们即使在一段平静期和友好关系声明之后，旧有的分歧也可能迅速重现。以弗所书2:14谈到雅伟拆毁了群体之间“仇恨的隔墙”，这对于长期存在争端的国家来说，是一个深刻的盼望。这一事件凸显了人类在拆除这些隔墙并真正睦邻友好方面所面临的持续挑战。

verse.textEn: For he himself is our peace, who has made the two groups one and has destroyed the barrier, the dividing wall of hostility.
verse.textZh: 因他使我们和睦，将两下合而为一，拆毁了中间隔断的墙。

summary.zh: 由学生发起的“蟑螂”运动正将其问责行动扩展至印度各地的政府学校。该运动此前因抗议考试丑闻导致教育部长于7月辞职而声名大噪。目前，活动人士正组织志愿者访问教室并记录教学条件，但他们的做法正面临政府当局日益增加的阻力。

body.en:
The student-led "Cockroach" movement is taking its campaign for accountability to government schools, but the activists' methods are encountering growing resistance from authorities.

The Indian activist movement dubbing itself the "Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)"  shot to national prominence in May by leading weeks-long protests over a scandal involving highly competitive entrance exams.

The student-led campaign put the government under intense political pressure and ended with the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan in July.

Now, the CJP is taking aim at India's government schools , organizing volunteer visits to classrooms, documenting conditions and demanding accountability for problems.

Launched on August 15, Independence Day in  India , the campaign asks parents, students and volunteers to inspect schools and record basic facilities including toilets, drinking water, electricity, classroom furniture and school buildings. The CJP has said the findings will be used to pressure authorities to make improvements.

The initial target is to audit 100 rural government schools over two months. It has also proposed giving recognition to village leaders who improve their schools.

Unlike the first campaign, which was based on street protests, the school audits require a more sustained form of local activism . Volunteers are expected to work consistently at the local level, document conditions and follow up with officials, parents and communities.

The organization is dealing with different layers of the Indian administration. Responsibility for government schools is divided between state governments, local administrations and elected village bodies. The CJP is therefore set to tackle different rules and political interests across the country.

India has over a million government schools, according to Education Ministry data. They make up nearly 70% of all schools in the country but serve less than half of its 247 million schoolchildren.

That scale has given CJP a vast field for its campaign. But it has also brought a new set of challenges.

The authorities are raising questions regarding rules and locations for the CJP scrutiny, as well as safeguards when children are present.

The response is already varying from state to state. Some authorities have ordered their own inspections, while others have restricted access or taken police action against CJP volunteers.

Authorities in Maharashtra and Rajasthan states have objected to school visits carried out without permission.

In one case, a complaint by school authorities resulted in police action against CJP members after they entered the premises to conduct an audit.

In Rajasthan, restrictions have been imposed on outsiders entering government...
body.zh: 学生领导的“蟑螂”运动正在向公立学校追究责任，但活动人士的方法正遭遇当局越来越大的阻力。 自称为“蟑螂简塔党 (CJP)” 的印度激进运动在 5 月份因涉及竞争激烈的入学考试丑闻而领导了长达数周的抗议活动，从而在全国引起了关注。 学生主导的运动给政府带来了巨大的政治压力，并以教育部长 Dharmendra Pradhan 于 7 月辞职而告终。 现在，CJP 正瞄准印度的公立学校，组织志愿者参观教室，记录情况并要求对问题负责。 该活动于 8 月 15 日印度独立日发起，要求家长、学生和志愿者检查学校并记录厕所、饮用水、电力、教室家具和校舍等基本设施。 CJP 表示，调查结果将用于向当局施压，要求其做出改进。 初步目标是在两个月内对 100 所农村公立学校进行审计。它还提议表彰改善学校的村领导。 与基于街头抗议的第一次活动不同，学校审计需要更持久的当地活动形式。 志愿者应在当地持续开展工作，记录情况并与官员、家长和社区进行跟进。 该组织正在与印度政府的不同层面打交道。公立学校的职责由州政府、地方行政部门和民选村庄机构负责。因此，CJP 将解决全国各地不同的规则和政治利​​益问题。 根据教育部的数据，印度有超过一百万所公立学校。它们占该国所有学校的近 70%，但为全国 2.47 亿学童中的不到一半提供服务。 这种规模为人民党提供了广阔的竞选空间。但它也带来了一系列新的挑战。 当局对 CJP 审查的规则和地点以及儿童在场时的保障措施提出质疑。 各州的反应已经有所不同。一些当局已下令自行检查，而另一些当局则对 CJP 志愿者实施限制或采取警方行动。 马哈拉施特拉邦和拉贾斯坦邦当局反对未经许可进行学校参观。 在一个案例中，学校当局提出投诉，导致警方在 CJP 成员进入校舍进行审核后对他们采取行动。 在拉贾斯坦邦，对外人进入政府施加了限制......

reflection.en: The 'Cockroach' movement’s insistence on auditing classrooms reminds us that education is not merely a bureaucratic service, but a sacred commitment to the next generation. When students themselves demand transparency in the face of institutional resistance, they echo the prophetic call for justice to flow unhindered like a river. True accountability...
reflection.zh: “蟑螂”运动对教室进行审计的坚持提醒我们，教育不仅仅是一项行政服务，更是对下一代的神圣承诺。当学生们在机构阻力面前要求透明度时，他们呼应了先知关于正义应如江河滚滚、不舍昼夜的要求。真正的问责需要有勇气记录那些令人不安的现实，以便为了弱势群体的利益，恢复公共服务的正直与诚信。愿雅伟赐予这些年轻人智慧，使他们在追求公义时既有热诚又有节制。

title.en: Nepal issues fresh flood warning as 3,000 still missing
title.zh: 尼泊尔发布新的洪水警报，仍有 3,000 人失踪

summary.en: Rescuers are trying to reach dozens of hydropower workers trapped in flooded tunnels, but have been hampered by further rainfall.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Rescuers are trying to reach dozens of hydropower workers trapped in flooded tunnels, but have been hampered by further rainfall.

The combined death toll from the devastating floods in Nepal  and Tibet rose to 750 on Sunday, with more than 3,000 people still missing, authorities said.

A fresh flood alert was issued after river levels rose again, while Tibetan authorities warned of a new barrier lake forming behind landslide debris.

Several scientists believe a glacier collapse in the Himalayas may have triggered Wednesday's disaster, sending huge volumes of water down a river valley.

Nepal's disaster authority put the number killed on its side of the border at 734, while Chinese state media confirmed 16 dead in Tibet, an autonomous region of China .

Chinese authorities said the dead included over a hundred Nepalis and people from more than a dozen countries.

The Nepalese disaster agency issued a warning for fresh floods on Sunday and told residents around the Bhotekoshi River to remain on high alert as water levels rose.

Flood warning notices were sent to residents' phones, advising them to move to higher ground.

On the Tibet side, Chinese state media said monitoring drones on Saturday night had picked up a new lake forming from a barrier created by a landslide near the Gyirong border port.

Rescue teams near the Gyirong border port were moved because of the risk of the barrier bursting.

Meanwhile, Nepalese rescuers are trying to reach more than 100 hydropower workers believed trapped and still alive in tunnels swamped by flood debris.

Rescue teams are focusing on several hydropower projects on the Trishuli River, where more than 900 workers went missing during the floods.

At one of the sites on Saturday night, army teams used drills to break into the upper part of a mud-swamped tunnel to pump oxygen and deliver a camera inside.

Nepal's prime minister's office said that teams faced "continuous rainfall and difficult conditions" but had worked nonstop overnight, "making tireless efforts to search for and rescue those who may be trapped."

Specialized teams from India and China have joined the rescue effort, along with Nepal's mountain rescue squad, which helps climbers on the world's highest peaks, including Everest.

Nepalese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Lok Bahadur Chhetri said the country needed assistance in such areas as tunnel rescue, DNA testing and identifying the victims.

The US State Department wrote on X that it would provide $3.6 million (€3.1 million) in "life-saving humanitarian assistance" to Nepal, including up to three months of emergency food aid for up to 10,000 flood-affected households.

body.zh: 救援人员正试图营救被困在被淹没的隧道中的数十名水电工人，但因进一步降雨而受阻。 当局称，周日尼泊尔和西藏特大洪水造成的死亡人数总计上升至 750 人，仍有 3,000 多人失踪。 河流水位再次上涨后，西藏当局发布了新的洪水警报，同时西藏当局警告说，山体滑坡残骸后面会形成新的堰塞湖。 一些科学家认为，喜马拉雅山的冰川崩塌可能引发了周三的灾难，大量的水流入河谷。 尼泊尔救灾当局称其边境一侧的死亡人数为 734 人，而中国官方媒体则证实中国自治区西藏有 16 人死亡。 中国当局表示，死者包括一百多名尼泊尔人和来自十多个国家的人。 尼泊尔救灾机构周日发布新洪水警告，并告诉博特科希河周围的居民，随着水位上涨，保持高度警惕。 洪水警告通知已发送到居民的手机上，建议他们转移到地势较高的地方。 在西藏方面，中国官方媒体称，周六晚上，监测无人机发现了一个新的湖泊，该湖泊是由吉隆边境口岸附近的山体滑坡形成的屏障形成的。 由于隔离墙有破裂的危险，吉隆口岸附近的救援队被转移。 与此同时，尼泊尔救援人员正试图救助 100 多名水电工人，据信他们被困在被洪水碎片淹没的隧道中，但仍然活着。 救援队正在重点关注Trishuli河上的几个水电项目，洪水期间该项目有900多名工人失踪。 周六晚上，在其中一个地点，军队使用钻头闯入一条泥泞的隧道上部，泵入氧气并在里面运送一台相机。 尼泊尔总理办公室表示，救援队面临“持续降雨和困难条件”，但连夜马不停蹄地工作，“不懈努力搜寻和营救可能被困的人员”。 来自印度和中国的专业团队以及尼泊尔山地救援队也加入了救援工作，该救援队为珠穆朗玛峰等世界最高峰的登山者提供帮助。 尼泊尔外交部发言人 Lok Bahadur Chhetri 表示，该国在隧道救援、DNA 检测和识别遇难者身份等方面需要援助。 美国国务院于 X 日写道，将向尼泊尔提供 360 万美元（310 万欧元）的“救生人道主义援助”，其中包括为最多 10,000 个受洪灾影响的家庭提供长达三个月的紧急粮食援助。 红十字会估计...

title.en: US news team attacked in occupied West Bank amid fresh settler violence
title.zh: 美国新闻团队在被占领的约旦河西岸遭受新的定居者暴力袭击

summary.en: Residents said masked settlers attacked Palestinian homes, trapping families and leaving several people injured.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Dozens of masked Israeli settler militants have attacked homes surrounding the occupied West Bank village of Qusra, the first major attack since a siege by settlers in the area earlier this month drew an international outcry .

The settlers surrounded a Palestinian home, throwing stones on Saturday while seven Palestinians were trapped inside, according to witnesses who spoke to Reuters news agency.

US news network NBC reported three of its members were also attacked while interviewing a Palestinian family in Jalud.

Saddam Oday, one of those trapped in Qusra, said the Israeli military fired tear gas into the home and detained the residents inside while letting him go. He said the Israeli military had not detained any of the settlers and had allowed them to leave.

The owner of the house, Luay Bayruti, said when the military arrived, they handcuffed, blindfolded and beat those inside, before later releasing them.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

The Israeli military said in a statement that troops and border police forces had arrived on the scene to remove "rioters" and protect the residents inside the house.

The military did not immediately respond to a request for comment on why they had reportedly fired tear gas at the house and detained and beaten the residents.

In his first public statement on Qusra, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said he condemned the violence in Qusra and blamed a "handful of rioters".

"I strongly condemn the criminal acts of violence committed in the villages of Qusra and Jalud," said Netanyahu, referring to the NBC news crew incident.

The United States had previously pressured Netanyahu to publicly condemn the militant settlers who had besieged Palestinians in their homes, US and Israeli officials told Reuters around two weeks ago.

The Israeli government has previously blamed a "fringe minority" for settler violence, a characterisation disputed by findings from rights groups.

A UN inquiry in June found that Israeli authorities are directly involved in settler attacks that have killed, injured and displaced Palestinians in the occupied West Bank. The Israeli mission in Geneva rejected the report's findings.

Bayruti said that after calling the Israeli military for help, he and six others were trapped inside the home for more than an hour as settlers threw stones.

Bayruti showed a Reuters reporter his bandaged arm, which he said had been injured by a stone during the attack.

Oday, a medic, said four of those trapped had suffered injuries due to the tear gas, and two had suffered injuries from the stones thrown by settlers.

The attack occurred a few hundred yards away from three homes to which settlers...
body.zh: 数十名蒙面以色列定居者武装分子袭击了被占领的约旦河西岸村庄库斯拉周围的房屋，这是自本月早些时候该地区定居者围困引起国际社会强烈抗议以来的首次重大袭击。 据路透社采访的目击者称，周六，定居者包围了一处巴勒斯坦人的房屋，并向其投掷石块，七名巴勒斯坦人被困在里面。 美国新闻网 NBC 报道称，其三名成员在贾鲁德采访一个巴勒斯坦家庭时也遭到袭击。 库斯拉被困人员之一萨达姆·奥代表示，以色列军方向屋内发射催泪瓦斯，并拘留了屋内的居民，同时释放了他。他说，以色列军方没有拘留任何定居者，并允许他们离开。 房子的主人卢艾·巴鲁蒂 (Luay Bayruti) 说，当军队到达时，他们给里面的人戴上手铐、蒙住眼睛并殴打，然后才将他们释放。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 以色列军方在一份声明中表示，部队和边防警察部队已抵达现场，清除“骚乱者”并保护房屋内的居民。 军方没有立即回应置评请求，询问他们为何向这所房子发射催泪瓦斯并拘留和殴打居民。 以色列总理本杰明·内塔尼亚胡在关于库斯拉的首次公开声明中表示，他谴责库斯拉的暴力行为，并指责“少数骚乱者”。 内塔尼亚胡在谈到 NBC 新闻组事件时表示：“我强烈谴责在库斯拉和贾鲁德村发生的暴力犯罪行为。” 美国和以色列官员大约两周前告诉路透社，美国此前曾向内塔尼亚胡施压，要求其公开谴责围困巴勒斯坦人家园的激进定居者。 以色列政府此前曾将定居者的暴力行为归咎于“边缘少数群体”，但人权组织的调查结果对这一定性提出了争议。 联合国六月的一项调查发现，以色列当局直接参与了定居者袭击，造成被占领约旦河西岸的巴勒斯坦人死亡、受伤和流离失所。以色列驻日内瓦代表团拒绝接受该报告的调查结果。 巴鲁蒂说，在向以色列军方求助后，他和其他六人被困在家里一个多小时，因为定居者投掷石块。 巴鲁蒂向路透社记者展示了他缠着绷带的手臂，他说他的手臂在袭击中被石头砸伤。 一名医务人员奥迪表示，其中四名被困者因催泪瓦斯而受伤，两人因定居者投掷的石块而受伤。 袭击发生在距离定居者居住的三所房屋几百码远的地方。

title.en: Number of missing Australians in Nepal rises, as China links disaster to climate change
title.zh: 中国将灾难与气候变化联系起来，尼泊尔失踪的澳大利亚人人数增加

summary.en: Australians are raising millions for Nepal disaster survivors as the death toll rises and thousands remain missing.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Australians have raised millions of dollars to assist survivors of the Nepal disaster, with many forced into temporary shelters amid mud and chaos.

Authorities said the death toll rose to nearly 800 on Sunday, with more than 3,000 people missing on both sides of the Nepal-China border after a torrent of ice, rock, mud and debris swept through mountain valleys and rivers on Wednesday, causing widespread devastation.

The federal government has announced a further $3 million in humanitarian support for Nepal, including supplies transported by the Australian Defence Force. It brings Australia's total assistance to $8 million.

The survivors remain in desperate need of basic amenities like clean drinking water and medical supplies.

Among them, Rabindra Hamal told the Australian Associated Press (AAP) news agency he and his colleagues working at a dam site were told to flee just minutes before the flood hit their area on Wednesday.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

They made their escape by car, but as they later tried to reach higher ground by foot, two of the group were swept away.

The group continued to scramble to safety but were forced to wait until the following day to be rescued.

They were flown by helicopter to a nearby army barracks and then evacuated to Kathmandu.

Hamal said that of the several thousand people working on the hydro project, about 500 were still missing.

As of Sunday evening, the number of missing Australians rose to 43, with the federal government continuing to do everything possible to confirm their welfare.

A public candlelight vigil will be held at Melbourne's Federation Square on Monday evening, in memory of those lost in the disaster.

A joint call for aid from the Emergency Action Alliance (EAA), made up of 15 prominent charities, has raised more than $3.5 million, including $2 million in contributions from the federal government.

The funding is going towards providing much-needed emergency shelter, food, safe drinking water, healthcare, hygiene and sanitation services, and supporting longer-term recovery assistance.

Save the Children is one of the organisations participating in the alliance, with the group's global media manager Amy Lefevre, visiting the affected Nuwakot district on Saturday.

"It's just mud everywhere, there's also a lot of confusion and chaos," she told AAP.

"It's just incredibly sad when you look around and you see someone's shoes stuck in the mud, or people's belongings strewn everywhere.

"It's very much still a rescue operation but of course, today is day five, and I think the chance of finding people alive is slowly dimming."

title.en: In Nepal's flood-ravaged towns, excavators drown out the sound of grief

summary.en: Nepal has requested specialized foreign assistance as the search for survivors resumes following devastating flash floods that killed hundreds and left thousands missing in a region bordering Tibet. Amidst the disaster, a missing Sydney woman, Cara Severino, was safely located after contacting her parents.

body.en:
In Bidur, Nepal, the sound of people crying is drowned out by the constant hum of excavators.

This town sits more than 45 kilometres from the site of Wednesday's glacial collapse, which triggered mudslides and flash flooding, killing nearly 700 people.

More than 3,000 remain missing, including 42 Australians in Nepal. Chinese state media on Sunday reported six Australians were also missing on the Tibetan side of the border.

In Bidur, the torrent of water was so powerful that it destroyed the winding road that once ran through it, as well as most of the buildings lining it.

Sticking out of the mud are the ruins of what were once homes and businesses; now nothing more than concrete shells covered in brown sludge.

Menuka Manandhar struggles down a ladder leaning against one of the buildings after searching the ruins of her home.

The layers of mud surrounding it are so thick, two men have to help lift her back to safety.

"All my things were inside the house. I could only take some important documents.

"I was here when the disaster struck, we escaped it by only a minute. We had barely crossed the road when it hit."

Other families emerge with a few small bags of belongings they were able to salvage from the higher floors of their buildings.

"Five people in our family were downstairs at the time of the flood," Ramji Lamsa, who was sheltering in a nearby school, said.

"I had a shop, a storehouse, and some vehicles. Everything was swept away. We don't have any resources to rebuild. We don’t know how the authorities are going to handle this."

Everything north of Bidur remains cut off by land. Nepali rescue crews are sending helicopters back and forth throughout the day, bringing back the injured and the dead they find on the other side.

Gaurav Thapa Magar was working in his bank at Timure, just three kilometres from the Tibetan border, when everything around him started shaking.

"In that moment, I just ran with everyone. And after I had taken five or six steps, I saw a big wall of water, almost three of four storeys of water, coming right after me.

"I felt like I was dead, to be honest. I was panicking, everyone was panicking, but I was really thinking 'I’m gone, I have to run, I’m gone'.

Gaurav spent most of the day waiting at the top of the hill he had climbed to, looking down on the wasteland that once was his town, until a helicopter arrived and evacuated him.

"When I looked down the whole village were swept away. And people were saying: 'There’s a body, there's a body'.

"There were so many people crying, who had lost their families. And there were so many people who were...

body.en:
Heavy rain is complicating an already difficult rescue effort, as hundreds remain missing three days after deadly flash floods hit the Nepal-Tibet border region.

The latest death toll from the devastating flash flood along the Nepal-Tibet border was reported on Saturday to be over 600, as frantic rescue operations to search for hundreds of missing people entered a fourth day.

Figures from both countries put the number of missing close to 3,000, with 682 bodies recovered and reports of corpses swept as far downstream as India.

According to Nepal 's disaster agency, the death toll there now stands at 675, with 2,426 people — including foreigners — still missing.

Across the border in Tibet, China's state news agency, Xinhua, has confirmed seven deaths and reported 554 missing individuals.

A glacial collapse on Wednesday sent rock, ice, mud and debris surging through the Himalayan mountain river systems below.

The flood swept through areas near the Chinese border, ravaging entire towns and damaging hydropower plants.

Nepal army spokesperson Raja Ram Basnet told the media on Saturday that helicopter operations were on hold until the weather improved.

Rescuers are battling thick layers of mud in the affected areas, which is making it difficult for helicopters to land and take off.

The army has located people trapped in a tunnel of the Trishuli 3A hydropower project in Nepal's Rasuwa District. Over 100 people are believed to be inside the tunnel filled with mud.

Basnet said that rescuers were struggling to locate the entry points of the tunnel and had made use of  baskets and ropes to reach some people. There are also limited places for helicopters to land in the area.

On Friday, Nepal's Army shared visuals of some people being rescued from the tunnel. The survivors were seen stuck in the mud, while officials crawled through the sludge and held out their hands to them.

On Saturday, Foreign Minister Shishir Khanal said a specialized tunnel rescue team had arrived from neighboring India and was ready to start work.

Nepalese authorities said the bodies of many flood victims have also been found dozens of kilometers from the disaster zone in Chitwan District in southern Nepal, which borders India.

Meanwhile, Indian authorities said they recovered the bodies of seven people who were swept downstream from Nepal and believe them to be flood victims.

Late on Friday, Nepal's Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal told the Reuters news agency that his country needed equipment, along with technical knowledge in tunnel rescue operations.

Khanal also told Reuters that Nepal did not need help with search and rescue operations but needed assistance in opening transport and communication lines in places...
body.zh: 大雨使本已困难的救援工作变得更加复杂，在致命的山洪袭击尼泊尔和西藏边境地区三天后，仍有数百人失踪。 周六，据报道尼泊尔-西藏边境毁灭性山洪造成的最新死亡人数已超过 600 人，搜寻数百名失踪人员的疯狂救援行动已进入第四天。 据尼泊尔救灾机构称，尼泊尔目前死亡人数为 626 人，仍有 2,426 人失踪，其中包括外国人。 在边境另一边的西藏，中国官方通讯社新华社已确认 7 人死亡，并报告了 554 人失踪。 周三的冰川崩塌使岩石、冰、泥土和碎片涌入下面的喜马拉雅山区河流系统。 洪水席卷了中国边境附近的地区，摧毁了整个城镇并损坏了水电站。 尼泊尔陆军发言人拉贾·拉姆·巴斯内特 (Raja Ram Basnet) 周六对媒体表示，直升机行动暂停，直至天气好转。 救援人员正在受影响地区与厚厚的泥浆作斗争，这使得直升机难以着陆和起飞。 尼泊尔拉苏瓦地区Trishuli 3A水电项目隧道内，军队已找到被困人员。据信，隧道内有超过 100 人，里面充满了泥土。 巴斯内特说，救援人员正在努力找到隧道的入口点，并使用篮子和绳索来救助一些人。该地区直升机的降落地点也有限。 周五，尼泊尔军队分享了一些人从隧道中被救出的画面。人们看到幸存者被困在泥里，而官员们则爬过污泥并向他们伸出双手。 尼泊尔当局表示，在与印度接壤的尼泊尔南部奇旺地区，距离灾区数十公里的地方也发现了许多洪水遇难者的尸体。 与此同时，印度当局表示，他们找到了从尼泊尔下游被冲走的七人的尸体，并认为他们是洪水受害者。 周五晚些时候，尼泊尔外交部长希西尔·卡纳尔告诉路透社，尼泊尔需要设备以及隧道救援行动的技术知识。 卡纳尔还告诉路透社，尼泊尔不需要搜救行动方面的帮助，但需要援助来开通桥梁被毁地区的交通和通讯线路、尸体身份识别、DNA测试以及尸体的长期储存。 路透社援引卡纳尔的话称：“我们已经在我们没有足够专业知识和技术知识的领域提出了此类专业服务和技术援助的请求。”

reflection.en: The devastating flash floods along the Nepal-Tibet border, leaving over 600 dead and hundreds missing, bring immense sorrow. In moments of such profound loss, the shortest verse in the Bible, "Jesus wept," reminds us that grief is a deeply human and even divine response to suffering and death. Our hearts go out to the families in the Nepal-Tibet border...
reflection.zh: 尼泊尔-西藏边境地区毁灭性的山洪造成600多人死亡，数百人失踪，带来了巨大的悲痛。在如此深重的损失面前，圣经中最短的经文“雅伟哭了”提醒我们，悲伤是对苦难和死亡的一种深刻的人性甚至神性的回应。我们的心与尼泊尔-西藏边境地区那些正在应对这场悲剧的家庭同在。

verse.textEn: Jesus wept.
verse.textZh: 耶稣哭了。

title.en: Footage of Tibet floods isn't being shown in China - and we know little about victims there
title.zh: 西藏洪水画面未在中国境内播放，受害者信息鲜为人知

summary.en: Dramatic footage of deadly flash flooding in Tibet, specifically at Gyirong Port, which swept away everything in its path and claimed hundreds of lives, has been largely hidden from public view and censored on the internet within China.
summary.zh: 西藏吉隆口岸发生致命山洪，洪水冲毁一切，造成数百人死亡，但相关震撼画面和信息在中国境内被大量隐藏，并在互联网上受到审查。

body.en:
The dramatic footage was almost impossible to miss. A torrent of water tearing through Gyirong Port, one of the main border crossings between Nepal and Tibet, sweeping away all in its path as hundreds of people fled for their lives.

The scenes, captured by CCTV cameras, quickly spread on social media and onto screens around the world.

Only a single still-frame shot has been broadcast so far by the country's state-run flagship news bulletin.

It has also been difficult to find the full video on China's heavily censored internet. Although various aspects of the disaster have been discussed online.

But what is even harder to find is any first-hand accounts of survivors describing the flash flooding that has claimed hundreds of lives, with just as many still unaccounted for since Wednesday.

Beijing has launched a massive rescue operation involving hundreds of emergency workers, which is continuing, and President Xi Jinping chaired an emergency meeting with officials to co-ordinate efforts.

But when you compare the country's internet content to what much of the world has been seeing online these past few days, China's firewall becomes more visible than ever.

Tibet, which Beijing annexed in the 1950s, had long resisted rule by the Chinese Communist Party.

China has quashed protests over the years, sometimes violently, and has been accused of grave rights violations in the Buddhist region. It has labelled the exiled spiritual leader, the Dalai Lama, a separatist.

That history means the very name Tibet draws China's censors. Beijing's sensitivities are especially apparent at times likes this.

There have been daily updates on the missing and the dead, and Beijing has also been posting updates on the rescue operations, as well as the dangers posed by a barrier lake that has been at risk of overflowing.

On Saturday, new footage from Chinese state media showed rescue teams wandering in a wasteland of mud and rock while calling out to anyone trapped.

But there is little detail beyond that. There are no accounts from survivors in Tibet, and almost no user-generated footage showing the deadly moments or their aftermath.

We are yet to hear from anxious families of those missing. Trying to contact people there is near-impossible during regular times.

As a journalist who has covered North Korea, it has often been easier for me to contact interviewees in Pyongyang than it is in the Tibetan capital, Lhasa.

On Thursday night, as global headlines led on the devastation in a Himalayan valley, China's state broadcaster opened its main bulletin with the launch of Xi's new book, a selection of his "most important and fundamental works".

Foreign journalists cannot travel to Tibet without government permission. We have just a few hours to get as much information...
body.zh: 戏剧性的镜头几乎不可能被错过。尼泊尔和西藏之间的主要边境口岸之一吉隆口岸发生洪流，洪水冲垮了沿途的一切，数百人逃命。 这些场景被闭路电视摄像机捕捉到，迅速在社交媒体和世界各地的屏幕上传播。 到目前为止，该国官方旗舰新闻公报只播放了一个静态画面。 在中国严格审查的互联网上也很难找到这段视频。同样很难找到描述这场夺去了数百人生命的山洪的帖子，自周三以来仍有同样多的人下落不明。 北京已启动了涉及数百名应急人员的大规模救援行动，该行动仍在继续，国家主席习近平主持召开了官员紧急会议，协调救援行动。 但当你将中国的互联网内容与过去几天世界上大部分地区在网上看到的内容进行比较时，中国的防火墙变得比以往任何时候都更加明显。 北京在 20 世纪 50 年代吞并的西藏长期以来一直反抗中国共产党的统治。 多年来，中国镇压了抗议活动，有时甚至是暴力镇压，并被指控在佛教地区严重侵犯人权。它给流亡精神领袖达赖喇嘛贴上了分离主义者的标签。 这段历史意味着中国审查机构用“西藏”这个名字来命名。北京的敏感性在这种时候尤其明显。 每天都有关于失踪和死亡的最新消息，北京也一直在发布救援行动的最新消息，以及堰塞湖面临溢出风险所带来的危险。 周六，中国官方媒体的新镜头显示，救援队在一片泥泞和岩石的荒地上徘徊，同时向被困人员呼救。 但除此之外就没有什么细节了。没有西藏幸存者的叙述，也几乎没有用户生成的视频显示致命时刻或后果。 我们还没有收到失踪者焦急的家人的消息。平时想要联系那里的人几乎是不可能的。 作为一名报道朝鲜的记者，我在平壤联系受访者往往比在西藏首府拉萨更容易。 周四晚上，当全球头条新闻报道喜马拉雅山谷的灾难时，中国国家广播公司以习近平新书的发布作为其主要公报的开篇，该书精选了他的“最重要和最基础的著作”。 未经政府许可，外国记者不得前往西藏。在视频被删除、声音被压制之前，我们只有几个小时的时间来尽可能多地获取有关此类重大事件的信息。 相反，我们必须依靠...

reflection.en: The tragic flash flooding in Tibet, particularly at Gyirong Port, has left hundreds dead or unaccounted for, yet dramatic footage and details remain largely hidden from the Chinese public. Proverbs 31:8 calls us to open our mouths for the mute, reminding us of the moral imperative to acknowledge and amplify the suffering of the vulnerable. Even when...
reflection.zh: 西藏吉隆口岸的洪水灾情造成数百人死亡或失踪，然而，相关的震撼画面和详细信息在中国公众面前却被大量隐藏。箴言31:8呼吁我们为不能发声的人开口，提醒我们有道德责任去承认并放大弱势群体的苦难。即使信息被压制，受苦者的呼声依然回荡，敦促我们为他们的困境发出同情和声音。

verse.textEn: Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, for the rights of all who are destitute. Speak up and judge fairly; defend the rights of the poor and needy.
verse.textZh: 你当为不能自辩的开口，为孤独的伸冤。你当开口按公义判断，为困苦和穷乏的辨屈。

title.en: Satellite images reveal scale of flood devastation in Nepal villages
title.zh: 卫星图像揭示尼泊尔村庄洪灾破坏规模

summary.en: Satellite imagery has revealed the scale of devastation along Nepal's Trishuli River following a deadly flash flood triggered by a glacier collapse on Wednesday. The torrent destroyed villages, bridges, and a key Nepal-Tibet border crossing, leaving hundreds dead and thousands missing.
summary.zh: 卫星图像揭示了周三因冰川坍塌引发的特大山洪对尼泊尔特里舒利河沿岸造成的破坏规模。洪流摧毁了村庄、桥梁和尼泊尔与西藏之间的一个关键边境口岸，造成数百人死亡，数千人失踪。

body.en:
New satellite imagery has revealed the scale of the devastation along Nepal's Trishuli River caused by Wednesday's deadly flash flood, triggered by a glacier collapse.

Before-and-after images show how sections of the valley, where a torrent of floodwater and debris surged through, destroyed villages, bridges and hydroelectric power stations.

Hundreds of people have been killed and thousands more are missing, Nepalese officials say.

Among the worst-hit locations reviewed by BBC Verify was a key Nepal-Tibet border crossing, which was engulfed by a rush of floodwater and captured on camera.

The satellite imagery from US-based intelligence firm Vantor, shows the site has been almost entirely washed away. Shocking CCTV footage showed the moment as the deluge of water swept over buildings as people tried to escape.

Damage and mud can be seen more than 2.5km (1.5 miles) upstream, reaching 100m (330 ft) above the area it first hit.

A few miles further south is the village of Timure, which has now largely disappeared.

The walls of the valley at this point are steep, reaching up to 50m above the water line. The image shows most of the houses perched on this slope are now gone or covered in mud.

A further 10km (eight miles) downstream, where the Trishuli River winds through Syapru Besi, satellite imagery now shows the village covered by mud, rock and other debris. Houses and other structures have disappeared, including bridges and a hydroelectric power station.

One of the larger villages to be struck by the full force of the flood was Trishuli, where some of the earliest verified footage of the disaster emerged from.

A satellite image of the town and surrounding agricultural land, which is about 45km (28 miles) downstream from the border, show an entire neighbourhood has been essentially washed away.

Verified videos of the town show a bridge collapsing as the river surges forward. At the very same moment from ground level, footage filmed from inside a bus shows people crying out in distress and trying to flee as they see the water rushing down the river.

Other dramatic videos show people sheltering inside a house, peering over the edge of a balcony as they watch a torrent of floodwater wash away almost everything around them, knocking large metal debris and a vehicle toward the building.

Somehow the house remains intact and survivors can be seen in a second verified video standing surrounded by mud once the floodwater had receded.

Imagery from satellite provider Planet Labs released today has also provided a clearer view of the disaster's origins at the collapsed glacier, the moment of which has been captured on a verified drone video.

The satellite image shows an enormous chunk of the glacier has fallen away, carving an enormous path of rock...
body.zh: 新的卫星图像揭示了周三冰川崩塌引发的致命山洪对尼泊尔特里苏利河沿岸造成的破坏规模。 前后照片显示了洪水和瓦砾汹涌而过的山谷部分地区如何摧毁了村庄、桥梁和水力发电站。 尼泊尔官员称，数百人死亡，数千人失踪。 BBC verify 审查的受灾最严重的地点之一是尼泊尔和西藏的一个重要过境点，该过境点被洪水淹没，并被摄像机拍摄到。 美国情报公司 Vantor 的卫星图像显示，该地点几乎完全被冲毁。令人震惊的闭路电视画面显示，当人们试图逃离时，洪水席卷建筑物。 在上游超过 2.5 公里（1.5 英里）处可以看到损坏和泥浆，到达其首次袭击区域上方 100 m（330 英尺）。 再往南几英里是蒂穆尔村，该村现已基本消失。 此时的山谷壁很陡，高出水线高达 50m。该图像显示，坐落在这个斜坡上的大多数房屋现在都已经消失或被泥土覆盖。 再往下游 10 公里（8 英里）处，Trishuli 河蜿蜒穿过 Syapru Besi，卫星图像现在显示该村庄被泥土、岩石和其他碎片覆盖。房屋和其他建筑物都消失了，包括桥梁和水力发电站。 Trishuli是遭受洪水全面袭击的较大村庄之一，一些最早经过核实的灾难镜头就来自那里。 该镇及周边农田（距离边境下游约 45 公里（28 英里））的卫星图像显示，整个社区基本上已被冲走。 经核实的该镇视频显示，随着河流汹涌澎湃，一座桥梁倒塌。就在同一时刻，从地面拍摄的公交车内拍摄的视频显示，人们看到河水顺流而下，痛苦地呼喊并试图逃跑。 其他戏剧性的视频显示，人们躲在房子里，从阳台边缘往外看，看到洪水冲走了他们周围的几乎所有东西，将大块金属碎片和一辆汽车冲向建筑物。 不知何故，房子仍然完好无损，在第二段经过验证的视频中可以看到洪水退去后幸存者被泥土包围。 卫星提供商 Planet Labs 今天发布的图像也提供了冰川崩塌灾难起源的更清晰视图，经过验证的无人机视频捕捉到了这一瞬间。 卫星图像显示，一大块冰川已经消失，形成了一条巨大的岩石道路……

reflection.en: The images of the Trishuli River valley being engulfed by debris remind us of the 'groaning' of a world subject to sudden, overwhelming natural forces. As we see homes and vital crossings washed away, we are confronted with the fragility of our earthly structures and the deep grief of those who have lost everything. We look to Yahweh to be near the...
reflection.zh: 特里舒利河谷被瓦砾和洪流吞没的景象提醒我们，受造之物在面对突如其来的巨大自然力量时正处于“叹息劳苦”之中。当我们看到家园和关键通道被冲走，我们直面人类建筑的脆弱以及那些失去一切的人们深重的悲哀。我们仰望雅伟，祈求祂亲近尼泊尔那些伤心的人，并为正在进行的搜救工作提供力量。

verse.textEn: We know that the whole creation has been groaning as in the pains of childbirth right up to the present time.
verse.textZh: 我们知道，一切受造之物一同叹息、劳苦，直到如今。

title.en: How Australians can help those impacted by devastating Nepal floods
title.zh: 澳大利亚人如何帮助受尼泊尔毁灭性洪水影响的人们

summary.en: Australian charities have launched a joint appeal to aid communities devastated by floods and landslides along the Nepal-China border. Thousands are in urgent need of shelter, food, clean water, and medical care after their homes and infrastructure were destroyed.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚慈善机构已发起联合募捐，以援助尼泊尔-中国边境受洪水和山体滑坡摧毁的社区。在房屋和基础设施被毁后，成千上万的人迫切需要住所、食物、清洁饮用水和医疗援助。

body.en:
Entire communities have been devastated by severe flooding and landslides along the Nepal-Tibet border, with homes, roads, bridges and critical infrastructure destroyed.

Search and rescue operations remain underway, while thousands of people are in urgent need of shelter, food, clean drinking water and medical assistance.

In response, 14 Australian charities have joined forces to launch a national appeal.

The Emergency Action Alliance (EAA) has launched the Nepal Flood Disaster Appeal, bringing together a variety of charities to support communities affected by the disaster.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

The alliance says donations will help provide immediate humanitarian assistance, including emergency shelter, food, safe drinking water, hygiene supplies and medical care.

Access to some affected communities remains difficult, with damaged roads and ongoing weather conditions hampering efforts to reach people in need.

Australians are encouraged to donate through the EAA website or by calling 1300 939 000.

The charities participating in the appeal are Save the Children Australia, Plan International Australia, Oxfam Australia, Australia for UNHCR, ActionAid Australia, CARE Australia, Caritas Australia, ADRA, Act for Peace, Anglican Overseas Aid, Australian Lutheran World Service, Baptist World Aid Australia, CBM Australia and Tearfund Australia.

EAA executive director Kerren Morris said the appeal provided Australians with a trusted way to support people affected by the disaster.

"Emergency shelter, food, safe drinking water and medical support are urgently needed now, while longer-term recovery efforts will continue for many months," she said in a statement.

The charities involved bring different areas of humanitarian expertise to the response, with organisations and their local partners working to provide immediate assistance to affected communities.

Save the Children is focusing on supporting children and families affected by humanitarian emergencies.

Oxfam Australia's humanitarian work includes support for essential services such as clean water, sanitation and emergency assistance.

Australia for UNHCR is the UN refugee agency's national partner in Australia, and is supporting humanitarian assistance through the UNHCR network.

The charities involved are continuing to assess the scale of the disaster and humanitarian needs in affected communities.

The EAA says its members are working to determine where support is most urgently needed as search and rescue operations continue.

The appeal has been endorsed by the Australian Council for International Development (ACFID), the peak body for Australian non-government organisations...

summary.en: While some people might be born with or develop certain traits, experts say it doesn’t mean they're destined for harmful behaviour.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Share your feedback and help us improve this feature. Read more about how we use AI at SBS here.

A man diagnosed with psychopathic traits, parents concerned about their children's violent behaviour, and guests who grew up believing they were bad. Are some of us born bad, or is harmful behaviour shaped by experience? How do nature and nurture influence our choices and morals? Watch Insight episode Born Bad? at 8.30PM Tuesday 1 September on SBS or SBS On Demand.

Loïc De Marie says he views a human as "a rock" and has struggled to understand other people's emotions from a young age.

"A little classmate died in a dramatic car accident when I was six years old … everybody was crying," the 26-year-old told Insight.

"This [was] the first time I understood that emotions are different with me [because] the look that the teacher gave me was, 'Why is this kid not crying?'"

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Growing up in Belgium, in that same year, Loïc and his little sister were playing near their backyard pool when she fell in.

"She was drowning, and I looked at her, and that was kind of troubling," he said.

He then saved her by holding out a plastic golf club for her to grab as he dragged her back to the ladder.

As he grew older, Loïc became increasingly involved in fights and would have angry outbursts.

"A guy was looking me in the eyes, some rivalry between men… and one day, I came to school with a baseball bat," he said.

Loïc says the police arrested him on the school grounds over the incident but says he never faced serious legal consequences.

Three years ago, Loïc began seeing a new psychologist — having grown tired of masking his thought processes.

The psychologist diagnosed him with antisocial personality disorder (ASPD) and documented traits associated with psychopathy — including manipulation and lying, a reckless disregard for other people's safety, and a lack of remorse and empathy.

"Everybody in the room can understand the words of the music and the melody ... I don't hear the melody — I don't understand it."

Loïc's father, Philippe, says he used to worry his son would go down the wrong path, but receiving a diagnosis was helpful.

"It [was] good to put a name on a disorder, and then you understand a lot of things.

"We try to ... do the best we can to support him [with] a lot of communication and love."

Forensic psychiatrist Dr Rajan Darjee, who has worked in prisons, mental health hospitals and in the community, says ASPD is a broad concept describing "people who, because of personality problems, are repeatedly breaking rules".

summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Share your feedback and help us improve this feature. Read more about how we use AI at SBS here.

In the case of Zomi Frankcom , an Australian killed in a drone strike while delivering humanitarian aid to the Gaza Strip in 2024, Israel's military justice system has concluded there is no reasonable suspicion of criminal misconduct.

It announced this month its decision to close the investigation into the death of Frankcom and six other World Central Kitchen (WCK) colleagues.

Israel's ambassador to Australia, Hillel Newman, said there had been no intention to attack the aid workers and a "reasonable mistake" was made.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

"There are tragic circumstances in a war zone and we're very sorry for the family, but that does not always mean that there's criminal liability," Newman told ABC Radio National.

Two Israel Defense Forces (IDF) officers were removed from their positions over the incident and another three were formally reprimanded.

But Foreign Minister Penny Wong has criticised the decision, noting "there are still many unanswered questions".

The Frankcom family and WCK are demanding an independent investigation into the airstrikes, saying "the IDF cannot credibly investigate its own conduct".

The case raises questions about whether Israel's military justice system is capable of delivering fair outcomes when its forces are accused of killing civilians, and where the line lies between a tragic operational error and conduct that warrants criminal investigation.

Michelle Burgis-Kasthala, professor of international law at La Trobe University, says there is "very compelling documentation" from many human rights organisations to suggest a "pattern of impunity" when it comes to the investigation of war crimes in Israel.

"A lot of the time they simply lapse and very rarely do they ever result in any form of criminal investigation, and even less likely [to result in] criminal conviction."

Last year, Action on Armed Violence (AOAV) looked at 52 publicly reported incidents in English-language media between October 2023 and June 2025, in which the Israeli media either reported an investigation was underway, or serious allegations of civilian harm.

The London-based charity found 88 per cent were either still under review or had been closed without any finding of wrongdoing.

So far, according to the cases examined by AOAV, only one case has resulted in a prison sentence against the accused.

title.en: 'Unsafe': Barnaby Joyce invokes disaster-hit Nepal to explain One Nation's refugee policy
title.zh: “不安全”：巴纳比·乔伊斯援引受灾的尼泊尔解释“一国党”的难民政策

summary.en: One Nation MP Barnaby Joyce suggested that Australia should not accept refugees from countries deemed unsafe for Australians to visit, citing flood-hit Nepal as an example.
summary.zh: “一国党”议员巴纳比·乔伊斯建议，澳大利亚不应接收来自政府认为对澳大利亚人来说不安全的国家的难民，并以遭受洪灾的尼泊尔为例。

body.en:
One Nation MP Barnaby Joyce has suggested that Australia should not accept refugees from countries that the government deems unsafe for Australians to visit, invoking flood-hit Nepal as an example.

Appearing on News24 (formerly Sky News) on Sunday morning, Joyce was asked whether Australia's current humanitarian intake should be cut.

Joyce brought up Nepal, which is reeling from catastrophic mudslides and flash flooding that have killed nearly 700 people. More than 3,000 more are missing, including 42 Australians.

"The refugee program has got to work within a policy structure we've got," Joyce said.

"Remember, we've clearly stated that if an area, the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFAT) says it's too unsafe to go there, then it's unsafe to bring people from there and away from there, such as places in Nepal.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

"I presume that the Department of Foreign Affairs says it's not unsafe to go to Nepal, but I wouldn't be going there at the moment."

Asked whether One Nation would stop accepting people from Nepal if DFAT were to advise against travel there, Joyce said he wasn't clear on DFAT's current position on the country, but "I know the Nepalese community have a huge say in sections of our country in the workforce, but they do it within the visa category."

"If they do come in, they'll be within the NOM," he added, referring to net overseas migration.

People who arrive on humanitarian visas currently contribute to net overseas migration figures.

While natural disasters can make a country unsafe to visit, people displaced by disasters do not generally qualify as refugees on that basis alone.

DFAT's latest travel advice for Nepal encourages a "high degree of caution due to the risk of natural disasters and road accidents". For certain areas closer to the disaster-hit region, it advises Australians to reconsider their need to travel.

Pressed on whether One Nation was happy with the current annual humanitarian intake level of 20,000, Joyce repeated that "it fits within the NOM".

"That is our policy, and the refugee policy — it's not that it's dispensed — but you can't come from countries which are dangerous. Like if you can't go there, you shouldn't be coming here."

Reporting suggested this week that the government intended to slash Australia's humanitarian intake by a third, however, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said on Thursday that humanitarian placements would remain at 20,000.

On Sunday, Social Services Minister Tanya Plibersek said that was a "permanent commitment".

There has been ongoing confusion over the specifics of One Nation's broader immigration policy.
